newsitem.title: JORDAN: EU says success of Euro-Med accords tied to reform.
newsitem.headline: EU says success of Euro-Med accords tied to reform.

text.p: The EU said on Saturday the success of its Euro-Mediterranean partnership policy to which it has already allocated over $6 billion in aid hinged on economic reforms by countries of the region.

"We all know that the success of the Euro-Mediterranean partnership largely depends on the outcome of economic reforms in the Mediterranean countries," Christos Papoutsis, member of the European Commission, told participants at the inauguration ceremony of the Medpartenariat fair held in Amman.

The fair is part of the Barcelona initiative agreed in 1995 which seeks to direct over $6 billion in European aid, soft loans and investment to Middle Eastern and North African countries by the end of the century.
The EU hopes to turn the Euro-Mediterranean region into a free trade area by 2010. It has already signed partnership accords with a number of countries and initialled one with Jordan.

Jordan is hosting over 500 European and Middle Eastern companies during the two-day EU sponsored fair which links small to medium sized private sector enterprises in Middle East and North Africa region (MENA) with European counterparts.
The event, previously hosted by Egypt and Israel, also aims to strengthen ties between the private sectors of the countries in the region.

Papoutsis said the EU had already allocated more than 4.7 billion Ecu ($5.2 billion) in grants to its Mediterranean partners and assigned more than 2.3 billion Ecu in loans to the region from the European Investment Bank.

"However this capital flow will not be sufficient. The success of the economic reforms also depends upon private capital flows. In fact the Euro-Mediterranean partnership relies to a large extent upon the private investor," Papoutsis said.
European entrepreneurs were upbeat about the economic propects of the region, enjoying a better investment climate and economic growth than it has for years, Papoutsis said.

"Most partner countries have stable currencies and prices and they apply active privatisation. Most of them are making impressive efforts to improve the regulatory and adminstrative environment for business," the EU official added. ($ = 0.904 European Currency Unit ECUs)
